meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 10: Debugging
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: A stdio server appears as 'failed' in the desktop host. Where do you look first, and what is in each file?

options.text: mcp.log for the server's stderr, and mcp-server-<name>.log for the host's UI events
mcp.log for connection events, and mcp-server-<name>.log for that server's stderr
The server's own stdout capture, since stderr is discarded by the host
The Inspector's session log, which is the only place connection errors are recorded

questions.explanation: The host writes general connection events to mcp.log and each server's stderr to mcp-server-<name>.log (macOS ~/Library/Logs/Claude/, Windows %APPDATA%\Claude\logs\). stdout carries protocol messages, not logs.

questions.question: Your server works in the MCP Inspector but fails in the desktop host. What has that told you?

options.text: Basic server operation is plausible, so look at host config, launch environment and versions
The Inspector bypasses the protocol, so the comparison proves nothing
The server is conformant, so the fault must be a bug in the host
The server only supports the Inspector's protocol era, so the host must be upgraded to match it

questions.explanation: Passing the Inspector narrows the fault domain: the server starts and speaks MCP. It does not prove every host integration detail, so the next suspects are absolute paths, env vars, the working directory and protocol-era or capability mismatches.

questions.question: A client complains that your HTTP server never sends notifications/message. What is the first thing to check?

options.text: Whether the request included io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel in its _meta
Whether the server declared the logging capability in server/discover
Whether the client opened a subscriptions/listen stream for log notifications
Whether the client called logging/setLevel during the handshake

questions.explanation: Log level is now per request: servers MUST NOT emit notifications/message for a request that did not include the logLevel key. logging/setLevel was removed, and log notifications travel on the originating request's stream, never the listen stream.

questions.question: The Inspector calls your tool successfully every time, but in the host the model never chooses it. Where is the fault?

options.text: In tools/list ordering, since hosts only expose the first few tools returned
In the tool's name, description and schema, which is all the model sees
In the host's authorization, which must grant a scope per tool before use
In the transport, since the host and the Inspector frame messages differently

questions.explanation: A working Inspector call proves the transport, the schema and the handler are fine, so the remaining variable is what the model reads: the name, description and inputSchema. Hosts do not silently truncate tools/list, and scopes gate access rather than selection.

questions.question: A request fails with 400 and -32602. Which cause fits?

options.text: The Mcp-Name header did not match the tool name in the body
The client declared capabilities but not the one this tool needs
The request omitted a required _meta field such as clientCapabilities
The server does not support the protocol version in the request

questions.explanation: A missing required _meta field makes the request malformed: -32602 with HTTP 400. An undeclared capability is -32021, an unsupported version is -32022, and a header that disagrees with the body is -32020.

questions.question: A dual-era client probes a stdio server with server/discover and gets JSON-RPC error -32601. What should it conclude?

options.text: The server is modern but does not implement discovery: retry with tools/list
The probe is inconclusive: retry the same request once more before deciding
The server is modern and the version was rejected: retry with a supported version
The server is legacy: fall back to the initialize handshake

questions.explanation: Modern servers MUST implement server/discover, so anything other than a DiscoverResult or a recognised modern error means legacy. Legacy servers answer unknown pre-initialize requests with implementation-defined errors, commonly -32601 or -32602, which is why the fallback MUST NOT be keyed to one specific code.

questions.question: A client sends MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18 to a server that implements only 2026-07-28. What comes back, and how is it different from -32020?

options.text: 404 with -32601, because the server has no handler for that revision's methods
426 with -32022, because the server is asking the client to upgrade the connection
400 with -32022, because the version is unsupported; -32020 means headers disagree with the body
400 with -32020, because any version problem is a header mismatch; -32022 is for bad transports

questions.explanation: -32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersion is returned with HTTP 400 when the advertised revision is not supported. -32020 HeaderMismatch is a different fault: the headers and the JSON-RPC body disagree, for example Mcp-Name not matching the tool in params.
